Every event in both clusters has event_source=FILE_SYSTEM, event_category=FILE_OPERATION, and the only event types present are MODIFIED (5 events at 1789924915) and CREATED (5 events at 1789924922). There are no ACCESS_CONTROL, BADGE, CARD, DOOR, LOGON, NETWORK, PROCESS or similar event types anywhere in the timeline, and no system_context is populated on any event. A ±86400 s temporal-neighborhood query around the activity anchor returns the same 10 file events only.

Targeted searches for badge-related evidence returned nothing: search_evidence with queries "badge", "door", "card scan access control entry" and an unfiltered search_evidence each returned total_count=0. get_existing_analyses returned 0 prior secondary analyses (faithful review state, nothing queued/rejected/invalid/failed).

Note on content: get_evidence at both digest and preview hydration levels returns content_preview="" and llm_summary/initial_summary=null for all five files, so file bodies were not recoverable through the available tools. However, the file names, extensions, sizes and category labels are themselves sufficient to establish the corpus is a small Chinese-language sales-script plus customer/deposit-record dataset, not an access-control log export.

Conclusion the records support: (1) there are zero door badge scan records in this task, so internal consistency of badge scans is neither established nor refuted — it is unanswerable from the available evidence; (2) no individual can be attributed as a badge holder, because no badge ID, card number, reader identifier, reader location, scan timestamp, or subject identity appears anywhere in the file inventory, the timeline, or the metadata; (3) the only events present are filesystem CREATED/MODIFIED operations on five unrelated business documents, with no actor attribution of any kind (no user, no account, no source IP, no process). Any positive claim about badge consistency or badge-holder identity would be unsupported speculation and is therefore not asserted.
